Evan — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: pricing step-downs are modest after 12 months; material uplift at 24 months. AWS PO activation: buyer uploads PO to Marketplace -> Seller (us) accepts -> then the subscription is activated for the buyer. The buyer still needs the PO; acceptance by the seller triggers provisioning.

I've attached a term/pricing matrix and a proposed approval path for multi-division buyers (see datascale_po_term_matrix.xlsx). High-level proposal:
- Default: 12-month auto-renew (finance signoff only)
- 12-18 months: Procurement + Budget Owner (no CFO)
- >18 months or >$1.2M TCV: Procurement + Budget Owner + CFO approval (or delegated finance director)

If you want to avoid CFO involvement we can structure a staggered activation: year 1 commit and prepay for core seats; year 2 optional add-on with capped uplift and an early-exercise clause. This typically keeps approvals at procurement + BU finance.

I'll leave details in the attachment and can set a 20-min call with Ben (pricing) and Vivek (co-sell activation) if you'd like.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Forwarding Evan's note and Olga's matrix. A couple of practical notes from pricing:

- 12m vs 24m: typical discount curve gives ~8-12% effective unit price reduction at 24m vs 12m once you factor in reserved capacity scheduling and lower per-token kernel cost (we modeled this in redwood_pricing_calc.pdf).
- To avoid CFO signoff we can use a split-invoice structure: prepay year1 (keeps procurement+BU finance), then year2 is an option with a capped renewal quote that procurement can approve within a specified window (90 days).
- If DataScale wants co-sell credits, they will need to register the opportunity in AWS and then we file co-sell. That part is separate from PO activation but often helps their internal commercial team sell the value — Vivek can lead that.

Action items I suggest:
1) Olga to propose split-invoice language and a short clause to include in the PO that commits buyer to year1 and leaves year2 as an option (legal-friendly).
2) Vivek to draft the AWS co-sell registration steps we need to do in tandem.
3) Tessa to confirm any Marketplace activation timing constraints from ops.

Ben

Maya — good questions. Answers based on ops/legal runbook:
1) AWS allows a single private offer to represent the committed volumes and term; split-invoice arrangements are permitted so long as the PO references the private offer ID and the invoicing schedule is specified in the PO. Operationally we record the invoicing schedule in our internal activation notes; AWS Marketplace itself will show the private offer as accepted once the seller accepts the buyer's PO.
2) Co-sell credits are tied to opportunity registration and revenue recognition windows, not strictly to year2 execution. If year2 doesn't execute, credits tied to year1 still apply (provided registration & co-sell conditions were met). We'll document co-sell acceptance criteria in the registration.
3) Early termination/proration: Redwood standard is 60-day notice with pro rata refund for unused prepayments beyond provisioning lead time. If DataScale requires alternative language we can negotiate (e.g., no refunds for prepaid core capacity).

Next steps I propose:
- I will produce a one-page PO template that references the private offer ID and spells out invoicing schedule + termination clause. (Deliverable: Olga — EOD Thu)
- Vivek will draft the co-sell registration checklist. (Deliverable: Vivek — Fri)
- Ben/Tessa will confirm activation lead times and whether ops needs any deployment hold windows.

If that works I can share the one-pager with your legal for a quick review and then we can create the private offer in AWS.

Thanks,
Olga
